clue.text: Game to make a hit with the knave of clubs

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players try to reach twenty-one

definitions.text: to make a hit with the knave of clubs
definitions.meaning: to strike someone with a cosh, read as the ..., the jack of a black suit such as clubs

explanation.surface: A card player's tip for scoring by playing the jack of clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the verb meaning to cosh someone, and on the knave of clubs being literally a black jack.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game twenty-one is also called this, and the verb means to strike with a short leather cosh.

clue.text: Sound vehicle for a parrot

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word as it is said, not as it is written

parts.note: a lorry is a goods truck, a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A loud truck turns out to be carrying a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: LORRY is the British word for a truck; said aloud it matches the name of a small brightly coloured parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The lory is a small Australasian bird of the parrot family.

clue.text: Vintage alternative to calves-foot jelly?

parts.note: an old-fashioned dish made from the foot of a grown bovine rather than a young one, stewed to a jelly

explanation.surface: A recipe book suggesting an old-style substitute for a traditional invalid's jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Calves-foot jelly is made from a young animal's feet; the older (vintage) beast's foot gives the alternative dish, a traditional British food.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewed foot of an adult bovine, jellied, was an old working-class British dish like the calf version.

clue.text: Just a way out mercenary old Latin poet

indicators.note: with the street taken away the word just loses those two letters

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
venal means open to bribery, motivated by money

explanation.surface: A hired soldier who is simply looking for an escape, described as an ancient Roman versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a way out' means JUST with a way (ST) taken out, leaving JU; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was the Roman satirist of the late first and early second centuries AD.

clue.text: Cut down church work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An instruction to fell something during church work.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with heavy strokes, as when felling a tree.

clue.text: Destined from the nursery to be a policeman?

definitions.text: Destined from the nursery to be a policeman?

parts.words: Destined from the nursery to be a policeman?
parts.note: a nursery-rhyme character whose colour suggests the police, the boys in blue

explanation.surface: A child marked out from infancy for a career in the force.
explanation.walkthrough: Police officers are 'boys in blue'; the nursery rhyme hero who blows his horn is a small boy of that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme figure who sleeps under a haystack fits a young lad bound for a blue uniform.

clue.text: Left to study at college-and played golf?

definitions.meaning: departed to take a programme of study
took to the links, a place for golf

explanation.surface: Someone who quit to attend college, or perhaps just spent the day on the links.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase covers enrolling on a programme of study and walking out onto a golf links.
explanation.definitionFit: Departing for training means attending a class programme; golfers also go out onto a links to play.

clue.text: But no small contributor to the fast food market

definitions.text: But no small contributor to the fast food market

parts.words: But no small contributor to the fast food market
parts.note: a kitchen appliance that heats meals quickly, though its name begins with a word for small

explanation.surface: A remark that some firm plays a big part in the takeaway trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The appliance makes food fast, and the joke is that it is no small contributor even though it opens with MICRO, meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen appliance cooks food rapidly, so it feeds the market for quick meals.

clue.text: Taken apart by the examiner

parts.note: a specimen cut up for study, or an argument picked to pieces by a critic

explanation.surface: A candidate's work is pulled to pieces by the person marking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The examiner may be a marker tearing an essay apart, but the literal sense is a pathologist cutting up a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut into pieces for scientific study, as a pathologist or biology student does.

clue.text: Suitable material for lightweight boxing

parts.note: a light stiff paper stock used to make boxes

explanation.surface: Advice on the right kit for a boxer in a light weight class.
explanation.walkthrough: Lightweight is a boxing weight class, but here boxing means packing things in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff pasteboard is the standard light material for making packing boxes.

clue.text: Letter from George Eliot all Greek to us

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A letter written by the novelist that is quite incomprehensible to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all Greek to us' points to a Greek letter, which is hidden across Eliot and all.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, also used to mean a tiny amount.

clue.text: She's capable of spinning a good yarn

definitions.text: She's capable of spinning a good yarn

parts.words: She's capable of spinning a good yarn
parts.note: the early multi-spindle spinning machine bears a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman who tells a fine story.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinning a yarn suggests storytelling, but the spinning jenny was the machine that spun thread for textiles.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning jenny, invented by James Hargreaves, spun several threads of cotton at once.

clue.text: Point to a covered walk

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A direction sign towards a sheltered path.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a colonnade or roofed portico was used as a public walkway.

clue.text: Wild cat I've caught out

indicators.note: out of order, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CT is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of trapping a feral feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IVE plus CT.
explanation.definitionFit: The civet is a wild carnivore of Africa and Asia, a cat-like mammal.

clue.text: Shellfish product found in a Cretan setting

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of words given
the words act as a setting, holding the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Something made by a mollusc turns up in a Cretan jewel mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is made by molluscs to line their shells.

clue.text: Places I set apart from others

indicators.note: the words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Seats I keep reserved, away from everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges PLACES I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something particular or exceptional stands out as different from the rest.

clue.text: Obtained information from nonsense writer Edward

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Gaining facts from the Victorian author of nonsense verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear is the nonsense writer, so 'Edward' looks like part of his name, but it is NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something out is to acquire knowledge of it.

clue.text: Intimate view of passengers on a charter flight?

definitions.text: Intimate view of passengers on a charter flight?

parts.words: Intimate view of passengers on a charter flight?
parts.note: a photograph taken from near at hand, and a description of travellers packed tightly together

explanation.surface: A peek at holidaymakers crammed into a cheap package plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Charter flights are notoriously cramped, so the passengers are packed tight; the film term is a shot taken from very near.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph or film shot taken at short range gives a detailed, intimate picture.

clue.text: Left our room, being below par

indicators.note: in a down answer the following pieces sit beneath the first

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who walked out of their home, feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being below' puts L and OUR beneath PAR in the down entry; 'below par' also means off-colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room in a house.

clue.text: Country originally brought to book

definitions.meaning: a goatskin leather, first from that country, used for binding books

explanation.surface: A nation first called to account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' usually means punished; here it is fine leather for bookbinding, first made in the North African kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African kingdom gave its name to the fine goatskin leather prized for bookbinding.

clue.text: He has setback in a race

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: he is a male

indicators.note: the word set is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner suffers a reverse during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE holds TES, from 'set' with 'back'; 'in' is a link. The race is the breed of small white dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed of toy dog from the Mediterranean island is one kind, and a race can mean a breed.

clue.text: Island masterful in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back, the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: able means skilled, masterful

explanation.surface: Looking back, a commanding island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island was Napoleon's first exile, a nod to 'masterful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's place of first exile, off the Tuscan coast, is an island.

clue.text: Question way to cook

definitions.meaning: to cook under direct radiant heat

explanation.surface: Asking how to prepare a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate hard is to subject someone to heat; cooking under a hot element is broiling.

clue.text: Tom's pleased, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Tom's pleased, by the sound of it

parts.words: Tom's pleased, by the sound of it
parts.note: a tomcat is male, and the noise it makes when content tells you it is happy

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom sounds happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name, but it is a tomcat, whose contented noise is a low vibrating rumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A contented cat makes a low continuous vibrating sound.

clue.text: Wimbledon champion on a quiet note

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A tennis star in a whisper.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tennis player Arthur took the 1975 men's singles title at the All England Club.

clue.text: Keen about being capped

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to be picked for the national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capped' suggests selection for a team; here it is the joint that has a kneecap. 'about' rearranges KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint is covered by a bony cap, the patella.

clue.text: Prominent feature of soap-box oratory

parts.note: the frank, forthright manner of speakers at open-air street meetings

explanation.surface: A remark on what stands out about street-corner speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: Soap-box orators stand up in public and speak their minds bluntly; 'prominent' also hints at standing out, OUT being part of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour in speech, saying plainly what one thinks, is typical of a street-corner orator.

clue.text: One willing to fetch and carry helps to win the game

definitions.text: One willing to fetch and carry helps to win the game

parts.words: One willing to fetch and carry helps to win the game
parts.note: a gun dog that brings back shot birds, recovering game for the hunter

explanation.surface: A dutiful team helper who contributes to a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetch and carry' suggests a servant and 'win the game' a sport, but game here is shot birds recovered by a gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun dog is bred to bring back shot birds, fetching them to the hunter.
